placements.why: The signed-manifest deployment gate is an architectural decision about release control — naming an organizational category the empty strata does not yet cover.
placements.title: Architectural decisions governing build, release, and deployment
placements.frame: What architectural choices shape how software is gated and shipped?

placements.title: From unsigned artifacts to signed-manifest gates
placements.frame: How does imposing a deployment gate function as both an enacted rule and a corrective response to prior security incidents?
placements.why: src-1 enacts the signed-manifest gate as a settled present-tense decision while src-2 justifies it by citing two unsigned artifacts that reached staging last quarter. Together they name a thematic subject — deployment gates as incident-driven security policy — that future envelopes can continue feeding with additional gate decisions and their incident justifications.
